headline: Weak quarter; growth getting shifted

highlights: EBITDA margin remained impacted by lower revenue booking from exports and higher execution from low-margin strategic NTPC order for CO2-based energy storage.

Going ahead, we expect TRIV to benefit from: 1) completion of NTPC order in 1-2 quarters, 2) execution ramp up from export orders, 3) qualification to bid for combined cycle data center orders post recent non-DC-led combined cycle order.
We expect the company to return to healthy growth and margin from FY28 onwards.
Results below our estimates TRIV reported revenue, EBITDA, and PAT below our estimates.
valuation: Financial outlook and valuation We cut our estimates by 17%/12%/9% for FY27/28/29E and expect TRIV’s revenue/EBITDA/PAT to clock a CAGR of 17%/15%/15% over FY26-29.
It follows average export pricing, with margins that are multiples of domestic margins, in a market dominated by gas turbine OEMs.
